result.note: Corporate pledge with a policy hook. Tested the Budget 2026-27 tax incentives for foreign cloud providers and the comparative Big Tech investment pledges.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the incentives for foreign cloud service providers in the Union Budget 2026-27:
items: It offers a tax holiday until 2047 on income earned by serving global clients through data centres located in India.
It provides a 15% safe-harbour margin on related-party transactions.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The Budget gave foreign cloud providers a 20-year tax holiday until 2047 on income from serving global clients via Indian data centres, along with a 15% safe-harbour margin on related-party deals. In June 2026, Amazon's enlarged India pledge followed these incentives, with its new tranche going to data centres in Mumbai and Hyderabad.
questions.source: which handed foreign cloud providers a 20-year tax holiday until 2047 on income earned by serving global clients through Indian data centres, plus a 15% safe-harbour margin on related-party deals

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs of companies and their India investment commitments as reported in June 2026:
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Microsoft's pledge is USD 17.5 billion, not USD 15 billion. Google committed USD 15 billion, and Amazon raised its total to USD 48 billion through 2030, a figure the Centre called a record. Amazon's total combines a fresh USD 13 billion with the USD 35 billion it pledged in December 2025.
questions.source: Microsoft has pledged USD 17.5 billion and Google has committed USD 15 billion on comparable horizons.
